```plato

    // One bend constraint projected: all four vertices displaced along their
    // own gradients, each by its inverse-mass share, in a single rebuild.
    // The leading 4 is the coefficient of the cited derivation; callers who
    // tune bending by feel fold it into `stiffness`.
    //
    // A configuration exactly folded flat (cosine = -1 or +1) has a vanishing
    // gradient and asks for nothing, which is correct: the constraint has no
    // preferred direction to unfold in.
    ProjectBend(vertices: Array<ClothVertex>, c: ClothBendConstraint, stiffness: Number): Array<ClothVertex>
    {
        var v1 = vertices[c.VertexA.Value];
        var v2 = vertices[c.VertexB.Value];
        var v3 = vertices[c.VertexC.Value];
        var v4 = vertices[c.VertexD.Value];
        var edge = v2.Position - v1.Position;
        var wingC = v3.Position - v1.Position;
        var wingD = v4.Position - v1.Position;
        var n1 = BendNormal(edge, wingC);
        var n2 = BendNormal(edge, wingD);
        var cosine = n1.Dot(n2).Clamp(-1.0, 1.0);
        var q3 = BendWingGradient(edge, wingC, n1, n2, cosine);
        var q4 = BendWingGradient(edge, wingD, n2, n1, cosine);
        var q2 = (BendEdgeGradientTerm(edge, wingC, n1, n2, cosine)
                + BendEdgeGradientTerm(edge, wingD, n2, n1, cosine)).Negative;
        var q1 = (q2 + q3 + q4).Negative;
        var share = v1.SolverInverseMass * q1.Dot(q1)
                  + v2.SolverInverseMass * q2.Dot(q2)
                  + v3.SolverInverseMass * q3.Dot(q3)
                  + v4.SolverInverseMass * q4.Dot(q4);
        var error = (cosine.Acos - c.RestAngle).Radians;
        var scale = SafeDivide(
            4.0 * (1.0 - cosine * cosine).Greater(0.0).Sqrt * error * stiffness,
            share, 0.0).Negative;
        return vertices.WithFourVertices(c,
            v1.Displaced(q1 * (scale * v1.SolverInverseMass)),
            v2.Displaced(q2 * (scale * v2.SolverInverseMass)),
            v3.Displaced(q3 * (scale * v3.SolverInverseMass)),
            v4.Displaced(q4 * (scale * v4.SolverInverseMass)));
    }

    // One Gauss-Seidel sweep over every bend constraint, folded exactly as the
    // distance sweep is.
    SweepBend(vertices: Array<ClothVertex>, constraints: Array<ClothBendConstraint>, stiffness: Number): Array<ClothVertex>
        => constraints.Reduce(vertices, (current, c) => ProjectBend(current, c, stiffness));

    // `iterations` bend sweeps.
    SolveBend(vertices: Array<ClothVertex>, constraints: Array<ClothBendConstraint>, iterations: Integer, stiffness: Number)
        : Array<ClothVertex>
        => iterations.MapRange(i => i)
            .Reduce(vertices, (current, i) => SweepBend(current, constraints, stiffness));

    // An empty bend-constraint array. The tree's constant idiom dispatches on
    // an ignored receiver of the result type; the result type here is a generic
    // `Array`, so its element type stands in, and it reads as
    // `ClothBendConstraint.NoBendConstraints`.
    NoBendConstraints(_: ClothBendConstraint): Array<ClothBendConstraint>
        => Repeat(0, ClothBendConstraint(
            VertexIndex(-1), VertexIndex(-1), VertexIndex(-1), VertexIndex(-1), new Angle(0.0), 0.0));

    //==
    // # Collision — sphere, plane, and any signed distance field
    //
    // Contact is one more position correction: push the vertex to the outside
    // of the collider and leave the previous position alone, so the Verlet
    // difference quotient turns the push into the velocity change a contact
    // should produce (the normal component is removed; the tangential
    // component survives, which is sliding).
    //
    // `offset` is how far outside the surface the vertex is left — pass the
    // cloth's `Thickness`, which is exactly what that field is for.
    //
    // These are three overloads rather than a collider interface. An interface
    // would earn its place if colliders had to be stored heterogeneously in one
    // array, but the three shapes share no state and no derived surface: each
    // body is two lines of its own geometry, and a caller composes contacts by
    // chaining `CollideWith`.

    // A point pushed out of a solid sphere onto the shell at Radius + offset.
    // A point exactly at the center has no direction to leave along and is
    // pushed along +Z.
    ProjectOutOf(self: Sphere, point: Point3D, offset: Number): Point3D
    {
        var away = point - self.Center;
        var reach = self.Radius + offset;
        return away.Magnitude >= reach
            ? point
            : self.Center + away.NormalizeOr(Vector3D.UnitZ) * reach;
    }

    // A point pushed to the front (positive-normal) side of a plane, `offset`
    // clear of it. The plane's signed distance is Dot(Normal, p) - Distance, as
    // `Plane` states.
    ProjectOutOf(self: Plane, point: Point3D, offset: Number): Point3D
    {
        var signed = self.Normal.Vector.Dot(point.PositionVector) - self.Distance;
        return signed >= offset ? point : point + self.Normal.Vector * (offset - signed);
    }

    // The central-difference gradient of a signed distance field, sampled at
    // +/- epsilon on each axis: six evaluations. For an EXACT distance field
    // the normalized result is the outward surface normal; for a field that is
    // only a lower bound it is a direction that leaves the surface, which is
    // all the projection below needs. A field that reports its own gradient
    // (`IDifferentiableSignedDistanceField3D`) should be asked for it instead.
    NumericalGradientAt(self: ISignedDistanceField3D, point: Point3D, epsilon: Number): Vector3D
        => Vector3D(
            self.Eval(point + Vector3D(epsilon, 0.0, 0.0)) - self.Eval(point - Vector3D(epsilon, 0.0, 0.0)),
            self.Eval(point + Vector3D(0.0, epsilon, 0.0)) - self.Eval(point - Vector3D(0.0, epsilon, 0.0)),
            self.Eval(point + Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, epsilon)) - self.Eval(point - Vector3D(0.0, 0.0, epsilon)))
            * SafeDivide(0.5, epsilon, 0.0);

    // A point pushed to where the field reads `offset`, one Newton step along
    // the numerical gradient. Exact for an exact distance field; for anything
    // else it is one iteration, and a deeply penetrating vertex needs the step
    // repeated.
    ProjectOutOf(self: ISignedDistanceField3D, point: Point3D, offset: Number, epsilon: Number): Point3D
    {
        var distance = self.Eval(point);
        return distance >= offset
            ? point
            : point + self.NumericalGradientAt(point, epsilon).NormalizeOr(Vector3D.Zero) * (offset - distance);
    }

    // Every cloth vertex pushed out of a sphere, by the cloth's own thickness.
    CollideWith(self: Cloth3D, sphere: Sphere): Cloth3D
        => self.WithVertices(self.Vertices.Map(v =>
            v.MovedTo(sphere.ProjectOutOf(v.Position, self.Thickness.Meters))));

    // Every cloth vertex pushed to the front side of a plane, by the cloth's
    // own thickness. A ground plane is Normal = +Z with Distance the height.
    CollideWith(self: Cloth3D, plane: Plane): Cloth3D
        => self.WithVertices(self.Vertices.Map(v =>
            v.MovedTo(plane.ProjectOutOf(v.Position, self.Thickness.Meters))));

    // Every cloth vertex pushed out of a signed distance field.
    CollideWith(self: Cloth3D, field: ISignedDistanceField3D, epsilon: Number): Cloth3D
        => self.WithVertices(self.Vertices.Map(v =>
            v.MovedTo(field.ProjectOutOf(v.Position, self.Thickness.Meters, epsilon))));

    // The mesh-bound forms: the face table is untouched by a contact.
    CollideWith(self: ClothMesh3D, sphere: Sphere): ClothMesh3D
        => ClothMesh3D(self.Cloth.CollideWith(sphere), self.Faces);

    // The mesh-bound plane contact.
    CollideWith(self: ClothMesh3D, plane: Plane): ClothMesh3D
        => ClothMesh3D(self.Cloth.CollideWith(plane), self.Faces);

    // The mesh-bound signed-distance-field contact.
    CollideWith(self: ClothMesh3D, field: ISignedDistanceField3D, epsilon: Number): ClothMesh3D
        => ClothMesh3D(self.Cloth.CollideWith(field, epsilon), self.Faces);
```
